_doc: Board facts for the pin allocator and safety check. Pin order is allocation preference. Capabilities: digital, pwm, analog, interrupt, i2c_sda, i2c_scl. Verified 2026-11-01 against the sources listed on each board; values under limits_notes marked 'SiliconLoop estimate' are design margins, not published specs.

uno.name: Arduino Uno

avoid_for_input.D13: on-board LED loads the pin, so pull-ups read unreliably

limits_notes.gpio_ma_absolute: ATmega datasheet absolute maximum, DC current per I/O pin (40 mA)
limits_notes.gpio_ma_recommended: ATmega datasheet test condition (20 mA at VCC = 5 V); used as the safe per-pin limit
limits_notes.mcu_total_ma: ATmega datasheet absolute maximum per VCC/GND pin (200 mA); applied to the whole chip, which is conservative on the Mega (4 VCC pins)
limits_notes.usb_5v_ma: SiliconLoop limit: 400 mA, below the 500 mA USB 2.0 rating, because board fuses, cables and laptop ports often deliver less (one source puts usable USB current on an Uno at ~400 mA)
limits_notes.board_self_ma: SiliconLoop estimate: the board's own draw (MCU, USB-serial chip, power LED)
limits_notes.rail_3v3_ma: SiliconLoop estimate: on-board 3.3 V regulator capacity
limits_notes.usb_peak_ma: SiliconLoop limit for brief worst-case peaks (servo stall/start-up): the board's 500 mA resettable USB fuse trips at roughly 1 A

sources: ATmega328P / ATmega2560 datasheets, Absolute Maximum Ratings

mega.name: Arduino Mega 2560

avoid_for_input.D13: on-board LED loads the pin, so pull-ups read unreliably
avoid_for_input.D20: I2C SDA has an on-board pull-up resistor that cannot be disabled
avoid_for_input.D21: I2C SCL has an on-board pull-up resistor that cannot be disabled
